brief.headline: Move them from 100% advance to 30-day credit and close the ₹12.95 L/year price gap to match Sayaji Industries

priceAsk.summary: Match the ₹66.48/KG we pay Sayaji Industries for the same Dextrose Anhydrous IP
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹70.80/KG — that's 6.5% more than our best price. The open-market asking band for this material runs ₹60–81/kg (typical ₹66–73/kg), so our target sits right in the normal range. We're overpaying, and three other suppliers already deliver at or below this level.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Switch from 100% advance payment to standard 30-day credit after delivery
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash that's currently locked up paying them in advance

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit is big — ₹1555.82 Cr in sales — but they keep only 2.9% of every ₹100 they sell, so there's not much profit to squeeze. They're growing fast (29.7%/year), which means they want more orders. We're tiny to them: our ₹1.06 Cr is just 0.07% of their business, so on our own we have almost no pull. The play is to bundle: commit longer volume in return for normal payment terms and the price we already pay elsewhere. Their health score is weak (D, 44/100), but they're not losing money — push firmly on terms and price, but don't corner them.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹70.80/KG; Sayaji gives us the same material at ₹66.48/KG
Closing that gap saves us ₹12.95 L every year
We pay 100% in advance right now; moving to 30-day credit frees up ₹8.73 L of our cash
They're growing fast, so they need new commitments
We're a tiny customer — just 0.07% of their ₹1555.82 Cr revenue
Their profit is razor-thin: they keep 2.9% of sales

alternates.name: Sayaji Industries Limited (current supplier)
alternates.why: Already delivers Dextrose Anhydrous IP at ₹66.48/KG — our benchmark and proof the price works

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health score B (62/100) — a drop-in alternate with strong financials; a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹842.97 Cr revenue, growing capacity — another credible second source; a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)

risks: We're only 0.07% of their business, so they can afford to walk away — bundle more volume or a longer commitment to get their attention
Their profit is just 2.9%, so pushing price too hard could hurt supply stability — lead with payment terms (where we give nothing up) and frame the price ask as 'match what we already pay elsewhere'
Their health score is weak (D, 44/100) — if they're cash-tight, a sudden switch to credit might spook them; phase it in (say, 50% advance now, 30-day credit in six months) if they push back
We have strong alternates lined up (Gulshan, Sanstar, Sayaji), but each needs qualification before we can switch — start that process now so the threat is real by next review
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and we'd like to lock in a longer commitment with you — but to do that we need you at the ₹66.48/KG we're already paying Sayaji, and on standard 30-day terms like our other suppliers.
